## Vertical Slice

The first end-to-end slice should include:

1. LL-01: verified environment.
2. LL-02: application shell.
3. LL-03: participant access.
4. LL-08: one session record.
5. LL-09: video playback.
6. LL-10: protected material download.
7. LL-14: access revocation.
8. LL-23: access and security test.

The vertical slice is the earliest evidence that the approved Option B boundary is technically viable. It does not authorize skipping the remaining work packages.

## Sequencing Logic

| Sequence | Work packages | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | WP-01, initial WP-07 | Environment, access, and security are prerequisites. |
| 2 | WP-03, WP-05 | Core training content, search, and filters preserve the original portal value. |
| 3 | WP-02, WP-04, WP-06 | Community, calendar, and administration complete the Option B experience. |
| 4 | WP-08 | Content must be loaded and checked before acceptance. |
| 5 | WP-09 | Full quality, participant testing, final acceptance, and fallback decision. |

## Conditional And Deferred Work

- LL-19 remains conditional until the video protection decision is made.
- LL-20 remains conditional until the SSO decision is made.
- RQ-19 capabilities are excluded and must not enter the backlog without an approved change.
- Individual work ownership remains `TBD` until the PM or team assigns it.

## Structure Acceptance

The structure is complete when every approved requirement has a work-package link, backlog item, dependency, and acceptance grouping; conditional and deferred work is visible; and no WordPress-only item is treated as the new app baseline.
